title: Keyboard manager mapping seems a bit laggy with left_alt

status.label: Retest held-Alt desktop switching on current stable
status.detail: The report has a precise sequence but uses PowerToys 0.62.1; it says the same mappings worked on 0.62.0.

judgment.rationale: The report gives two mappings from Ctrl+Win+Left/Right to Alt+X/C, then says that while holding left Alt, pressing C and then X without releasing Alt no longer switches desktops; it worked on 0.62.0 but fails on 0.62.1. There are no comments or current-build tests. The sequence is specific enough to ask for a current retest and confirm whether the failure occurs after the first mapped shortcut or only during rapid alternation.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.62.1 and says the same behavior worked on 0.62.0.
Two desktops are used; Ctrl+Win+Left maps to Alt+X and Ctrl+Win+Right maps to Alt+C.
The reported sequence holds left Alt, presses C, then presses X without releasing Alt; the second desktop switch fails until Alt is released and pressed again.
The report mentions LibreOffice Writer 7.4.0.3 but says the behavior occurs in any window; there are no comments or assignees.
A repository search found no matching report for this exact held-Alt alternating desktop-switch sequence.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask whether the exact sequence still fails on v0.102.3001 and whether releasing left Alt after the first switch restores the second mapping.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report may reflect a held modifier or shortcut invocation state that is not reset between sequential mapped desktop-switch shortcuts, but current behavior must be confirmed first.

proposed_fixes.title: Investigate repeated desktop-switch mappings while Alt remains held
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The first remapped Alt+X/C shortcut may leave the shortcut invocation or modifier state active, preventing the next remapped desktop-switch sequence until Alt is released; this is unverified on current stable.
plan: Retest the exact two-desktop configuration and held-Alt sequence on v0.102.3001.
Record whether the first switch succeeds, whether left Alt remains logically active, and whether releasing it restores subsequent switches.
If reproduced, trace shortcut state reset between the two remapped desktop-switch inputs and add a regression test for alternating actions under a held modifier.
verification: Confirm repeated desktop changes can be triggered by alternating X/C while left Alt remains held.
Verify the mappings continue to work after ordinary modifier release/repress cycles.

confidence.rationale: The old report provides exact steps and a version regression, but there is no current-build confirmation or evidence of the state left after the first switch.
